analyst_view.overall: Leaders Almería (1st, 35 points) host Nicolás Larcamón's Sporting Gijón (10th, 23 points) on Sunday; the numbers make Almería clear favourites with about 3.1 goals. Almería won 3-2 at Ceuta on 23 November (Sergio Arribas twice, Chumi's header from an Arribas corner) for a third straight win and the top spot back, though lately they have taken fewer shots and corners than usual and let opponents shoot more (Ceuta had 18 shots to their 14), which the numbers already count. Stefan Dzodic is banned (counted); Nico Melamed is still training apart, Rodrigo Ely and Pulido missed Wednesday's session and Chirino is available again, per Noticias de Almería. Sporting have one win in five, lost 0-2 at home to Las Palmas with five yellow cards, lose right-back Guille Rosas to a ban (counted) and have had a long injury list all autumn (Gelabert, Konrad de la Fuente, Antonio Casas, Pablo García), already visible in their recent results. No referee is named yet; nothing I found goes beyond what the numbers know, so I stay with them on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 2.1 for Almería, already allowing for Dzodic's ban (small, -3.2%), Rosas's absence at the back for Sporting (+6.2% for Almería) and his share of Sporting's goals (-12.6%). Almería have scored 13 in six and Sporting have conceded freely, while Melamed's absence has lasted weeks and is in their recent form; I stay at about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, already cut for Almería's low recent corner count (14 in six, -5.2%) and raised for Sporting's, as Almería have conceded 44 in six. Almería still score from corners (Chumi's winner at Ceuta), but nothing new points to a different count, so I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards, 3.6 for Sporting, already raised 12% for their recent bookings (five yellows against Las Palmas, Rosas's fifth among them) and a little for past meetings. Sporting chasing the game against the leaders could add fouls, but that is how the numbers already see it, and no referee is named yet, so I stay at about 5.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, already lowered for Almería's quieter recent shooting (58 in six, -9.1%) and lifted for Sporting's (+19%), as Almería have let opponents shoot 111 times in six. Sporting's injuries in attack (Gelabert, Casas, Konrad) have lasted weeks and are in those figures, so I stay at about 27.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target, 5.8 for Almería, whose recent accuracy dipped a little (-2.0%) while Sporting's rose (+7.7%). Arribas is in form and Chirino returns for Almería, but neither changes what the numbers expect; I stay at about 10.
